Mathematically, this is captured by a Lagrangian framework: L = U(x) - λ(C(R(x)) + μ·(∑x_i - X_max)), where λ and μ are shadow prices. Optimizing yields a marginal rate of substitution between certainty and utility that equals the ratio of marginal costs. This implies a structural duality: efficient uncertainty reduction equates the marginal cost of certainty across different sources of uncertainty. Failure occurs when agents ignore the convexity of C, leading to either over-investment in low-hanging fruit or neglect of tail risks.
